source.paper: Vending-Bench: A Benchmark for Long-Term Coherence of Autonomous Agents
source.status: Original Vending-Bench was deprecated by Andon Labs on 2025-11-18 in favor of Vending-Bench 2, while the original page remains as a historical leaderboard.

artifact_evidence.official_executable_release: No public AndonLabs Vending-Bench repository was located in the AndonLabs GitHub organization or linked from the primary paper/page in this audit.
artifact_evidence.operator_repeated_runs: Andon Labs continued running the original benchmark on newer frontier models through 2025 and publicly updated the leaderboard. These are repeated first-party benchmark executions, useful for temporal robustness but not independent replication.
independent_recreations: nathanwjclark/vending-bench-clone explicitly says it is an independent rebuild from public information and is not affiliated with Andon Labs.
markattarcolgate64/open-vending-bench describes itself as an open-source recreation and still-in-progress implementation.
letterj/vending-bench is an independent vending-machine benchmark implementation focused on Grok 4 Fast, with its own Docker/uv environment and recorded result files.
artifact_evidence.recreation_scope: These recreations demonstrate that the general vending-business task family is implementable, but because the exact original simulator/supplier behavior/prompts/demand dynamics are not proven identical, their outputs cannot be treated as replications of the original paper's model rankings/failure rates.

paper_claims.horizon: Original paper reports runs exceeding 20M tokens while agents manage inventory, ordering, pricing and fees over long simulated business horizons.
paper_claims.failure_modes: Primary paper reports high run-to-run variance and derailments from delivery-schedule misinterpretation, forgotten orders and tangential/meltdown loops from which agents rarely recover.
paper_claims.context_window_result: Primary paper reports no clear correlation between failure onset and the point at which the context window becomes full; this supports the bounded claim that observed breakdowns were not explained solely by context-window exhaustion in those runs.
paper_claims.temporal_extension: First-party later leaderboard runs show newer models can materially improve reliability/profitability while still leaving substantial spread and headroom, but those later cells are not part of the original paper experiment.

reproducibility_assessment.official_artifact_support: strong primary paper/operator reporting, weak public exact-simulator replayability
reproducibility_assessment.judgment: Vending-Bench is valuable failure evidence because it exposes long-horizon coherence breakdowns over very long trajectories and Andon Labs repeatedly exercised the benchmark on later models. Reproducibility of the exact original environment is nevertheless limited: no official public simulator release was identified, and the open GitHub implementations found are explicitly recreations or separate experiments rather than provenance-equivalent copies. Therefore the qualitative failure family and first-party longitudinal leaderboard are well documented, while exact model comparisons, failure timing and no-correlation statistics remain tied to the primary operator's environment.
exact_blockers: No official Andon Labs source repository for the original Vending-Bench simulator was found in targeted web/GitHub search.

Exact supplier simulation, demand/weather dynamics, agent prompt/tool schemas, environment randomness/seeds and historical model API versions are therefore not reconstructable from an audited official code commit in this pass.
The original benchmark is now deprecated in favor of Vending-Bench 2, so current first-party evaluation development no longer targets exact original-environment maintenance.

Independent GitHub projects explicitly label themselves clones/recreations or implement different simulator/model assumptions; their successful runs cannot be mapped directly onto original Vending-Bench paper cells.
Hosted model versions used in 2025 are moving external dependencies, so even a faithful environment recreation would require exact provider/model snapshot provenance for numerical replication.
No independent study was located that reproduced the original paper's correlation analysis between context-window saturation and failures using the provenance-equivalent original simulator.
reproducibility_assessment.scope: Retain Vending-Bench as strong observational evidence that long-horizon agent failures can arise without a simple context-window-full trigger. Do not infer that context capacity never matters, that all meltdown modes share one cause, or that independent vending-benchmark recreations replicate the original environment.

downstream_note: The highest-value reusable evaluation idea is longitudinal variance/failure recovery, not the vending domain itself. A target-system adaptation should preserve repeated seeded runs, explicit event logs for orders/deliveries/state changes, failure-onset localization, and analysis against active-context occupancy while using an environment whose full transition code and seeds are versioned. This can test whether context management reduces meltdown without relying on the unreleased original simulator.
